speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing fatigue, lower leg swelling, and weight loss. To begin our investigation, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any changes in your appetite or urination patterns?

speaker: Patient
text: 66-year-old white male. The patient reports a 10-day history of fatigue and bilateral lower leg swelling. He mentions a weight loss of 3.6 kg (8 lbs) over the past 6 months without trying. He has a history of chronic bronchitis and uses an albuterol inhaler as needed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of chronic bronchitis and recent weight loss alongside leg swelling, have you experienced any shortness of breath, coughing up blood, or decreased appetite recently? REQUEST TEST: Basic_Metabolic_Panel, Liver_Function_Tests, TSH.

speaker: Doctor
text: The metabolic, liver, and thyroid panels are all normal. Given your 10-day history of bilateral leg swelling and recent weight loss, have you noticed any shortness of breath, orthopnea, or frothy urine? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray, Abdomen_US.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue. I also have Lower leg swelling, Unintentional weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial labs and imaging are normal, which helps rule out common cardiac, hepatic, and thyroid causes. Given your 10-day history of bilateral leg swelling and unintentional weight loss, have you noticed any skin changes like redness or warmth in your legs, or any pain with walking? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, D-Dimer, ECG.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Nephrotic Syndrome (likely Membranous Nephropathy given the age and weight loss). The 4+ proteinuria, fatty casts, and hypoalbuminemia (implied by edema) confirm renal involvement. While the elevated D-Dimer suggests a high risk for pulmonary embolism due to the hypercoagulable state associated with nephrotic syndrome, the clinical picture is dominated by renal failure.
